title: Week 42: Reliability Engineering and Safe Recovery Checkpoint

questions.prompt: Checkpoint: Why inspect other threads for an ANR?
questions.explanation: The main thread may be waiting on a lock, binder or worker whose stack reveals the actual causal dependency. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
options: Classify the ANR, reconstruct the causal thread dependency and remove blocking from the responsiveness path.
questions.answer: Classify the ANR, reconstruct the causal thread dependency and remove blocking from the responsiveness path.

questions.prompt: A low-memory kill always produces a catchable OutOfMemoryError in the app.
questions.explanation: It shows the allocation that finally failed, while earlier retention or native/graphics growth may have consumed the memory. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.

questions.prompt: Complete the operational rule: Why is jitter essential during widespread failure?
questions.explanation: It desynchronises clients so they do not retry together and recreate the overload spike. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
questions.answer: It desynchronises clients so they do not retry together and recreate the overload spike.
acceptedAnswers: It desynchronises clients so they do not retry together and recreate the overload spike.
